entries.title: Proverbs 4:1
segments:
CHAP. IV. 
 
  An exhortation to the study of wisdom, is forced by various arguments,   ver. 1-13.   A caution against bad company, ver. 14-19.   Directions for the attaining and keeping of wisdom, ver. 20-27. 
 
  V. 1. A father-Of me, who have paternal authority over you and affection for you.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:3
segments: V. 3. Tender-Young and tender in years, and tenderly educated. Only beloved-Beloved above all the rest.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:4
segments: V. 4. Said-The following verses, at least as far as the tenth verse, are the words of David.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:7
segments: V. 7. With all-Even with the price of all.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:8
segments: V. 8. Exalt-Let her have thine highest esteem and affection.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:9
segments: V. 9. Grace-A beautiful ornament, such as they used to put upon their heads.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:16
segments: V. 16. For-They cannot sleep with quietness.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:17
segments: V. 17. For-Wickedness is as pleasant to them as their bread.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:18
segments: V. 18. But-Just men daily grow in knowledge, and grace, and consolation, 'till all be perfected and swallowed up in glory.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:19
segments: V. 19. Darkness-Full of ignorance and error, of uncertainty and confusion, of danger and misery.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:23
segments: V. 23. Heart-Thy thoughts, will, and affections.  For-From thence proceed all the actions, as of the natural, so of the spiritual life, which lead to eternal life.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:24
segments: V. 24. Mouth-All sorts of sinful words.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:25
segments: V. 25. Right on-Direct all thine actions to a right end, and keep thy mind fixed upon that way which leads to it, and neither look or turn aside to the right-hand or the left.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:26
segments: V. 26. Ponder-Consider thine actions before thou dost them, and see that they agree with the rule.  And-Let thine actions be uniformly and constantly good in spite of all temptations.
